title: Google Flow film

stages.name: Premise
stages.deliverable: Story hook, cast, conflict, ending, emotional intent and target runtime.
stages.instruction: Propose a few distinct ideas. Ask the director to select or revise one before adaptation. Use yt-script for scored hook options and yt-package for the click promise; use yt-viral only when research is requested. Register supporting notes; they do not replace the premise deliverable.

stages.name: Comic
stages.deliverable: A readable 10-page comic with approved visual direction and initial character designs.
stages.instruction: Calibrate a visual sample first. Preserve approved premise. Register the pages as one versioned package.

stages.name: Script
stages.deliverable: Complete screenplay, scene intent, continuity and shots grouped into packages up to 15 seconds.
checks: Dialogue and action fit the planned durations
stages.instruction: Adapt the approved comic into a screenplay. Use natural shot lengths; a generation package is not necessarily a visible cut. Read yt-script and score hooks using hookscore.py. Retain beat/on-screen directions and actual source pins; a YouTube script does not bypass the approved ten-page comic or full screenplay.

stages.name: Audio
stages.deliverable: Measured temporary dialogue, isolated character tracks, silence/action beats and cue sheet.
stages.instruction: Use the scratch audio tool. Listen in context. Preserve the full line on overflow and request timing changes.

stages.name: Boards
stages.deliverable: Labeled boards plus clean frames, character/prop references and exact reference mapping.
stages.instruction: Keep permanent character IDs. Include emotional direction and scene start/end state. Review exact prompt and asset versions together. Consider yt-package for the thumbnail visual brief while preserving the storyboard/reference deliverable.

stages.name: Blender
stages.deliverable: Color-coded dummy scene, editable Blender file and clean playable preview against approved timing.
stages.instruction: Use approved shots and timing. Render a picture-only reference and review copy. Do not treat technical render success as approval.

stages.name: Google Flow
stages.deliverable: Original generated takes, exact submitted prompt/settings, pinned references, observed provider receipt and take review.
stages.instruction: Pin the approved prompt, ordered clean references, measured audio and Blender previs. Inspect the signed-in Google Flow visible browser UI for current capability and settings. Review timing adaptations, then obtain an exact-version credit/attempt allowance before Generate. Record every attempt, provider evidence and original download; reconcile unknown outcomes before any retry. Human take review is required. The Flow film adapter is not implemented; never substitute Wan.

stages.name: Edit
stages.deliverable: Selected take timeline, finished film, separate audio, captions and portable project export.
stages.instruction: Use approved usable ranges. Compare transitions and pacing across packages. Keep source takes and editable timeline. Use yt-edit with an actual timed transcript, yt-seo for search-facing delivery text and yt-package for title/thumbnail checks. Use yt-chapters only for eligible long-form transcripts and yt-shorts only when repurposing actual long-form sources. Post-release yt-comment, yt-retention and yt-audit require real audience/channel inputs. Supporting skill output does not replace the reviewed final film.

timing_note: The diagram plans 2–15 whole-second packages at 30 fps. These are planning constraints, not a guarantee of Flow model capability; inspect live controls and review any adaptation.

diagram_mapping.package: flow: pinned exact prompt, references, approved audio and previs; capability preflight
diagram_mapping.spend: flow: human exact-package budget and attempt allowance before Generate
diagram_mapping.wan: flow: Google Flow browser execution; test shot then authorized batches
diagram_mapping.takes: flow: original downloads, provider receipt and human take review
